title: GameCore catalog pack
description: One emulator or application = one directory. seed/, logo.png|logo.svg, generator.py and tests/ are implicit: they are present on disk or they are not, and no field declares them.

emulatorName.description: The product name, when it differs from the platform label: `label` is 'Nintendo 64', this is 'Rosalie's Mupen GUI'. Shown by the graphical installer, which used to carry its own copy of both. Absent = fall back to `label`.

family.description: Who made the hardware: 'Nintendo', 'Sony', 'Microsoft', 'Sega'... The installer groups the catalogue by it, so a box with twenty systems reads as four short lists instead of one long one. Free text on purpose — a pack for a machine nobody here anticipated names its own maker and is grouped with its siblings without a line of UI changing. Absent = grouped under 'Other'; apps are grouped by their kind and ignore this.

description.description: One line shown next to the tick box in the install wizard.

order.description: Where this system sits in the grid, and in the installer's tick list. A curated running order, not alphabetical — the console you reach for most is first. Absent means last, in id order: a pack that forgets it is placed badly, never dropped. Before this field the order was a list of ids inside scripts/gen-catalog.py, and a pack missing from that list was silently absent from both the grid and the installer.

sharesEmulator.description: The pack that owns the emulator this system runs on, when one emulator serves several systems (Dolphin: GameCube and Wii). The two declare the same `install` and `launch`; only the owner may carry `config`, `controllers`, `seed/` and `generator.py`, because they write the emulator's own files. `scripts/check-catalog.py` allows a shared Flatpak app id only between packs linked this way.

supersededBy.description: The packs that replaced this one when it was split into one pack per system (dolphin → gamecube, wii). A superseded pack is never offered by the installer or added to a grid; it stays so a box that still has its tile keeps launching it until the owner runs `scripts/split-systems.py`.

windows.description: Rewritten for GameCore for Windows. Only these packs get a tile on a Windows grid (update/finish.py, run by the installer and after each update); the Linux packs stay in the tree as test data until each one is ported (dev log D57). Absent = Linux pack.

install.description: How the MAIN artifact is obtained. Extra system dependencies go in `packages`, never here.

appIds.description:
Ordered candidates, best first. The installer takes the first one the remote still offers; everything else on the box takes the first one actually installed.

A list and not a string because an upstream can vanish overnight — Ryujinx original left Flathub with no warning, and Ryubing is one maintainer's decision away from the same. With a single id that day broke twice and said neither: the install found nothing, and the tile went on launching a name that no longer existed. A second candidate is the difference between a degraded box and a dead slot.

One entry is perfectly legitimate: it means nobody has found a credible alternative yet, not that the pack forgot.

sandbox.description: Flatpak override. Absent = the emulator policy (filesystem @GAMECORE_PATH@, device all, socket x11). Only meaningful when install.provider is flatpak.

formerArgs.description: Launcher args this pack shipped before its emulator changed (the Switch: Eden's `run @APPID@ -f -g`, which Ryujinx reads as a graphics backend). A tile still carrying one is rewritten by the update merge (backend/services/catalog/merge.py); any other args are the operator's and stay.

fullscreen.description: For a window no CLI flag makes fullscreen (Stremio has none; Lutris's nested gamescope ignores -f under KWin). backend/services/fullscreen_enforcer.py waits for a window whose WM_CLASS matches, then asks the WM to fullscreen it over EWMH.

gamepadTrigger.description: Re-fire udev after launch. A Flatpak app that opens its own window only sees a pad plugged in before it started; this makes one plugged in after it appear. Needs the udevadm sudoers rule.

preferIfPresent.description: Absorbs the REWRITE pass of flatpakify-systems.sh: when this path exists, it wins over the nominal launcher.

showExtension.description: Whether the library shows each game's file extension. Absent = true. False for a system whose entries are not dumps but pointers to a game installed elsewhere (`.lutris` stubs): the extension tells the player nothing, and the listing sends an empty `ext` (backend/services/pack_library.py).

consoles.description:
The DISTINCT MACHINES this one emulator runs, when it runs more than one. Omit it — as eleven of the thirteen packs do — and the emulator is its console; nothing downstream changes.

Declared because it cannot be derived. `scraper.libretro` is a list of names in libretro's database and the database does not enumerate consoles: melonDS declares 'Nintendo - Nintendo DS' AND 'Nintendo - Nintendo DS (Download Play)' for one machine. `scraper.mediaAlias` really is one entry per console but it is ScreenScraper's vocabulary, spaces and all ('nintendo 64'), so it is somebody else's name to rename. And `roms.extensions` cannot answer either: `.zip` is declared by nearly every pack and says nothing about its contents, `.iso` serves GameCube and Wii alike, and `.rvz` is Dolphin's own container which holds either — `gamemedia/registry.py` carries the scar, every Dolphin game was once looked up as a GameCube game.

What this buys: a bezel per console. mGBA runs Game Boy in 10:9 and Game Boy Advance in 3:2 behind one system id, so one frame cut for one of them bites into the other — and the drift correction, keyed by the announced ratio, was learned once and applied to all three.

Claim only the extensions that BELONG to one console. Leaving `.iso` unclaimed is the honest declaration, not a gap: an unclaimed extension resolves to no console and the cascade stays at the system level, exactly as before.

id.description: Short, stable, and answerable to nothing outside this repository — which is what lets it be part of a filename (`mgba.gba.png`) and of a drift-correction cache key without a rename elsewhere breaking both. No dots: the bezel filename is `<system>.<console>.png` and one there would make it unparseable.

ratio.description: The aspect this machine renders at, as W:H (10:9, 3:2). Optional, and declared only when it is one answer: mGBA's consoles each have exactly one; dolphin's run 4:3 and 16:9 both, so they rightly say nothing. Consumed by the overlay slots endpoint so a manager UI can warn when a deposited bezel's measured hole does not match the machine — without it the mismatch is only discovered in game.

extensions.description: Must all appear in `roms.extensions`, and no two consoles of a pack may claim the same one — `scripts/check-catalog.py` fails the build on either.

bios.description:
The system files the OWNER has to supply, and where they go. Nothing here is ever downloaded, shipped or linked to — this block only says what a working install looks like, so `backend/services/bios.py` can answer 'absent / wrong md5 / conforming' instead of the emulator answering with a black screen.

The information was already in the seeds, unreadable: `catalog/pcsx2/seed/PCSX2.ini` has named `ps2-0150e-20001228.bin` since the first release, and nothing could check whether that file was on the box. A player whose PS2 games all failed to boot got no message naming it.

Declare only what is SOURCED — a filename a seed pins, or one the emulator itself defines. A guessed name produces a permanently red line on a working install, which is the ticket this block exists to remove.

dir.description:
Where the files belong, as a path expression. `@FLATPAK_CONFIG@` and `@FLATPAK_DATA@` expand from the same `install.appIds` entry the box actually has installed — the gopher64 rule — so a BIOS directory under an app id nobody installs is unexpressible. `@HOME@` and `@GAMECORE_PATH@` are also accepted, for the emulators that are not Flatpak.

This is NOT `config.dest`: PCSX2 reads its inis from `PCSX2/inis` and its BIOS from `PCSX2/bios`, Cemu keeps `keys.txt` under data/ and its settings under config/. Deriving one from the other would have named the wrong directory for both.

files.description: The files checked by name. Omit for a system whose emulator scans the directory instead — see `anyFile`.

file.description: Name relative to `dir`, subdirectories allowed. Never absolute and never containing '..': the checker refuses to stat outside `dir`, and a pack that tried would be reading a path the catalogue does not own.

md5.description: Expected fingerprint, when a single dump is the right one. Absent means 'present is all we can check' — a firmware whose hash changes with its version (RPCS3, Ryujinx keys) must NOT carry one, or every legitimate update would be reported as corrupt.

required.description: true = the system does not work without it, and a launch is refused with this filename on screen. false = the install is fine without it (regional firmwares, high-resolution BIOS, keys only some titles need). Red on a working box is the ticket this block was written to stop, so `false` is the answer whenever there is any doubt.

note.description: One line the player reads. What the file is for, never where to get it.

anyFile.description: For an emulator that SCANS `dir` and takes whatever image it recognises — DuckStation's `[BIOS] SearchDirectory`. No filename can be checked because the pack legitimately pins none, so the only honest verdict is 'the directory has something in it' or 'it is empty'. Never carries an md5, for the same reason.

config.description: Where seed/ is deployed. Omit entirely when the pack ships no seed/.

nativeDest.description: Destination when launch.path is not 'flatpak' (mgba, melonds).

order.description: Where this emulator sits in a profiling pass, and therefore in the toast the player sees when a pad is plugged in. Absent means last, in id order. It used to be a tuple of ten ids in backend/services/configgen/__init__.py, and a pack missing from it was never profiled at all — its bindings silently never written.

strategy.description: How apply_profile dispatches, not a summary of what the pack writes. rewrite-player-block: rpcs3 · rewrite-device-line: dolphin (binds by NAME) · guid-rebind: ryujinx (binds by GUID) · sdl-index-clone: pcsx2/duckstation · snapshot-restore: azahar/mgba/cemu/gopher64 — generate() is called for every connection and owns the whole decision, which for gopher64 means restoring a snapshot OR writing RMG's generic profile into that player's port · snapshot-or-synth: melonds — the dispatcher asks snapshots.exists() first, which only works for a pack whose extract/replace are not per-player · none

multitap.description: The accessory a two-port console needs before slot 3 exists at all. `value` turns it on, `offValue` turns it back off. Both are declared here because a release that had to GUESS the off value would be inventing config, and because the tap belongs to the roster rather than to a slot: nothing switched it off for a long time, so every solo session after one session at four ran with a virtual accessory on port 1.

offValue.description: What the key reads when no player needs the tap — the value the seed ships.

padType.description: The Type= value that keeps sticks and rumble alive (pcsx2 DualShock2, duckstation AnalogController).

seedMustNotContain.description: Python regular expressions (re.M) a seed/ may never match. Regexes, not plain substrings: RPCS3 YAML structurally needs a `Device:` key, and what must be forbidden is a Device that NAMES a controller, not the key itself. A seed that names a device pins the grid to one controller model; CI fails on a hit.

usb.description:
The peripherals this system needs that are NOT SDL gamepads: the GameCube adapter Dolphin drives over raw libusb, a DolphinBar, an arcade stick that enumerates as a keyboard, a wheel, RPCS3's DS3 passthrough.

None of them can enter the roster through `controllers`, and that is the point. `gamepad_monitor` only ever sees a device that declares BTN_SOUTH on an evdev node, so an adapter with no evdev node at all was invisible everywhere: no line on the controllers screen, no udev rule, and no way for the owner to tell 'not plugged in' from 'not supported'.

Declaring one here does four things: it lays the rule down at install (`installer/applier.py`), it lists the device on the controllers screen present-or-absent, it re-fires udev after launch so a device plugged in later reaches the Flatpak sandbox, and it puts the pack's own note on screen when the device is missing.

It never refuses a launch. A USB accessory is optional by nature — Dolphin plays fine with a DualShock 4 — and blocking would be inventing a fault, the mistake `bios.required` exists to avoid.

vidPid.description: Lowercase `vendor:product`, exactly as sysfs writes it in /sys/bus/usb/devices/*/idVendor. Pinned lowercase so a pack and a udev rule that name the same adapter in different case are still the same adapter.

class.description: What KIND of thing it is, which is what the roster was missing. `gamepad` is the case the pipeline already handled; the other four are the ones it could not express. The controllers screen groups by it, and it is the honest answer to 'why does this device not get a player slot' — a light gun never should.

label.description: What the owner calls it — 'GameCube adapter', 'DolphinBar'. Absent = the vidPid is shown, which is correct but unreadable from a sofa.

udevRule.description:
One udev rule line, written to /etc/udev/rules.d/99-gamecore-<pack>.rules at install. Omit when the device needs no rule — plenty work on their kernel defaults, and an unnecessary rule is a permission widened for nothing.

Write the narrowest rule that works: this grants access to a device node, and `MODE="0666"` on a device that also carries a keyboard interface is every keystroke on the box readable by any local uid. The existing 99-gamecore-input.rules documents that trade at length.

note.description: One line the player reads when the device is not detected. What it is for and what to check — the mode switch on a DolphinBar, the USB port a passthrough needs. Never where to buy one.

localMedia.description: The on-disk layout this system's dumps use, so icons, titles and disc serials can be read from the game files themselves instead of guessed from the filename. Absent = this system has no local media and falls back to online scraping, which is exactly what an emulator nobody listed used to get. WHICH parser reads a format is code (backend/services/local_media.py); WHICH format a system uses is this. duckstation and pcsx2 read the identical PlayStation layout and differ by one string — that was six `if sid == …` branches across three functions before it moved here.

format.description: ps3: PS3_GAME/ICON0.PNG + PARAM.SFO · ps4: sce_sys/ · psp: the same two files inside the ISO · gcwii: the 6-char id in the image header · playstation: the serial in SYSTEM.CNF. A new format is new code, so this enum only grows alongside local_media.py.

discTag.description: The kind `disc_id()` returns, when it is not the format name. gcwii reads GameCube and Wii images alike but reports 'wii'; duckstation and pcsx2 share the playstation parser and report 'psx' and 'ps2'. Absent = the format name.

profileSaves.description: How this emulator keeps each profile's saves apart. Absent = one save shared by every profile, as before profiles existed. Only the pack that owns the emulator declares it; a pack that `sharesEmulator` follows its owner. Three forms. An object with `keys` and/or `dirs` (most emulators, no code): the save options to point at the profile's folder (`@SAVES@`) and the folders with no option, swapped for a symlink to it; the primary profile keeps the emulator's own values and folders (backend/services/profile_save_paths.py). `per-instance` / `p1` with a `place_saves(dirs, root, opts)` hook in generator.py, for a layout that needs code (melonDS: one instance per player). `{supported: false, why}`: the saves cannot follow a profile, and why, so Settings can say so.

config.description: Relative to the pack's config directory (native or flatpak, as configgen resolves it); `..` allowed.

section.description: INI section; absent for a flat file (RetroArch).

value.description: `@SAVES@` is the profile's folder. A value without it (`true`) is set as is.

quote.description: Write the value in double quotes.

config.description: Relative to the pack's config directory (native or flatpak, as configgen resolves it); `..` allowed.

as.description: Name of the profile's folder for it; default: the folder's own name.

optional.description: Skip it when its parent folder is missing (one of two layouts an emulator has used). At least one entry must apply.

perGame.description:
Whether this emulator can be configured ONE GAME AT A TIME, and if so where that file goes.

The cases this exists for are binary, not cosmetic: an RPCS3 title that sits on a black screen until Write Color Buffers is ticked, a Dolphin game that freezes on anything but Vulkan, a Wii U dump whose textures are garbage without its graphic pack. The difference is not 40 fps against 60 — it is starts against does not start, and from a sofa the only remedy was to leave GameCore, find the emulator's own window, and hunt.

REQUIRED on every emulator pack, and the requirement is the point. An emulator that cannot do this must say so with `supported: false` and a reason, because the failure mode of leaving it out is silence: the button is absent, the player cannot tell 'this emulator has no per-game settings' from 'GameCore forgot this emulator', and neither can anyone reading the catalogue.

And because it is DATA, the day shadPS4 grows per-title configs is a pack.json pushed down the signed OTA channel — not a release, not a frontend build, not a box reboot. That is the whole reason this block is here and not in a table in backend/services/.

why.description: Why not, in one line, when `supported` is false. What is missing — an identity nobody can read out of the dump, a per-game path nobody has verified on a real install. Never 'not implemented': that is the one thing the reader can already see.

path.description:
Where the per-game file lands, as a path expression, with `@GAMEID@` standing for whatever `key` resolves to. Same expander as `bios.dir` and `config.dest` — `@FLATPAK_CONFIG@` expands from the `install.appIds` entry the box actually has installed, so a per-game directory under an app id nobody installs is unexpressible.

This is NOT derived from `config.dest`. RPCS3 keeps its custom configs beside its main one under config/, Dolphin keeps GameSettings/ under data/, and an emulator that put them somewhere else entirely would have no way to say so.

`@GAMEID@` is mandatory, and the pattern is what enforces it. A path without it names ONE file for every game on the system — which is not a smaller version of this feature, it is the exact bug the feature exists to remove, wearing its interface: the player sets Vulkan on one game and silently sets it on all of them.

format.description: How the file is written. `ini` is [section]/key = value; `yaml` is the two-level mapping RPCS3 uses. A new format is new code in backend/services/pergame.py, so this enum only grows alongside it — the same rule `localMedia.format` follows.

key.description:
Which reader in backend/services/gameid.py names the game. The enum mirrors that registry exactly and test_pergame_contract.py fails the build when the two drift, because a `key` the registry does not implement is a per-game file that is never written and never explains why.

When the pack also declares `localMedia.format`, the two must be the SAME string: a ROM whose identity is one thing to the scraper and another to the config is a bug nobody would find by reading either.

settingsArgs.description:
The arguments that open this emulator's OWN settings window, where the player picks the setting GameCore then keeps.

GameCore deliberately builds no unified settings screen. Translating 'internal resolution' into thirteen vocabularies, and then maintaining that translation across every emulator release, is exactly what makes Batocera's configgen impossible to port — so the button opens the real thing instead.

Declared rather than derived. The obvious shortcut is to take `launch.args` and strip `--fullscreen --no-gui`, which is a hardcoded list of other people's command-line flags living in the backend: it works for the three emulators somebody checked and silently opens a fullscreen game with no window for the fourth. The pack knows its own launcher.

Absent = no button. An emulator with no settings window to open must not be offered one.

merge.description:
What happens to a per-game file that already exists. `own-keys`: read it, set only the keys GameCore was asked to set, leave every other byte alone — the same divergence from Batocera the controller generators make, and here it protects settings the player made in the emulator's own window.

One value, deliberately. A second one is a second write path, and it gets added the day an emulator actually needs it and can be tested against that emulator, not in advance.

profiles.description:
Known-good settings for named titles, shipped as data so they ride the signed catalogue channel. This is the 'it just works' half: the player launches, the game starts, and nothing on screen mentions that a setting was placed.

Versioned by emulator on purpose. The day RPCS3 renames an option, an unversioned profile stops being help and becomes a trap — it keeps writing a key that no longer exists while the screen still says the profile is applied.

gameId.description: Exactly what `key` resolves to for this game — a Title ID, a 6-character disc id. Not a title: two dumps of one game share an id and disagree about their filename.

label.description: The game's name, for the one line the player reads when they go looking.

why.description: What breaks without it. 'Black screen until Write Color Buffers is on' — the sentence that lets someone judge whether removing it is safe.

emulator.description: The emulator versions these settings were verified against, as `>=x.y.z` or `>=x.y.z,<a.b.c`. A profile whose range excludes the installed emulator is offered but NOT applied automatically, and says so.

settings.description: section → key → value. One nesting level, because both supported formats have exactly one: an INI section, or a YAML top-level mapping.

steamStore.description: PC games only: after a scrape, read the minimum system requirements from the public Steam store (title search, then appdetails) into `meta.requirements`. Opt-in because a console game has no PC spec, and a store hit by name on one would print a wrong one. See backend/services/gamemedia/steam_store.py.

overlay.description: Bezel identification only. window_rect and hole stay in config/overlays.json: they are image/resolution tuning, not a property of the emulator. `label` is NOT repeated here - the pack's own label is used.

packages.description: Extra system dependencies, NOT the main artifact. Aggregated across all selected packs into a single pacman call.

sources.description: git_sync semantics: clone when absent, pull --ff-only otherwise, never over local changes.

ifAbsent.description: Write only when dest does not exist. For a file the owner is expected to hand-edit: re-running the installer is documented as safe, and for the demo EmberTV config that has to mean untouched.

hostAccess.description: Fixed host prerequisites for user daemons. Applied as root; stripped from untrusted packs. ptrace permits same-user process memory access globally (Yama scope 0).

gamemode.description: Adds the gaming user to the `gamemode` group the gamemode package creates. Its polkit rule lets only that group switch the CPU governor and renice games; without it gamemoded starts and changes nothing.

services.description: User units only. arch.sh:668 documents why creating this tree as root broke the kiosk.

postInstall.description: Last resort, bounded: runs as the user, never root, with a timeout, and a failure NEVER interrupts the install - it logs a warning. An ordered list, because some apps need two irreducible steps (generate a cert, then trust it).
